title: Natural coproduct truncation exact-couple comparison
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] admitting derived categories and K-injective right derived functors [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be left exact and additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let $I$ be a small set, $K_i,S\in D(\mathcal A)$ and $u_i:K_i\to S$ such that $H^r(K_i)=H^r(S)=0$ for $r<a$, for a common integer $a$. Put $G_n=H^n RF$ and $P_{p,r}(L)=H^p(RF(H^r(L)[0]))$, with maps induced functorially. There exist type-zero bigraded exact couples $X,Y$ [def-sp-exact-couple] in $\mathcal B$ and a couple morphism $T:X\to Y$ [lem-sp-derived-couple-functoriality] with: $X.D^{p,r}=Y.D^{p,r}=0$ for $r<a$; $X.E^{p,r}=Y.E^{p,r}=0$ for $p<0$; for every integer $n$, isomorphisms $e_X^n:X.D^{0,n}\cong\bigoplus_iG_n(K_i)$ and $e_Y^n:Y.D^{0,n}\cong G_n(S)$ under which the canonical map $\bigoplus_iG_n(K_i)\to G_n(S)$ is $(e_X^n)^{-1}$ followed by $T_D^{0,n}$ followed by $e_Y^n$; and for every $p\ge0,r\in\mathbf Z$, isomorphisms $s:X.E^{p,r}\cong\bigoplus_iP_{p,r}(K_i)$ and $t:Y.E^{p,r}\cong P_{p,r}(S)$ such that $T_E^{p,r}$ is $s$ followed by the canonical map $\bigoplus_iP_{p,r}(K_i)\to P_{p,r}(S)$ followed by $t^{-1}$. No hypothesis that these canonical maps are isomorphisms is imposed.

source.place: Tag 015J hypercohomology second page and abutment; Tag 05TC derived lower bounds and truncation comparison; Tag 08DZ direct-sum spectral-sequence reduction; parent construction steps 1 and 2

proof.text: Represent the cohomologically bounded-below objects by bounded-below complexes of injectives; lift each derived morphism into the target injective representative. Apply the truncation hypercohomology construction to each representative. Its exactness and canonical structure-map descriptions identify the resulting triangle maps. Naturality of canonical truncation triangles, followed by the triangulated right derived functor and homology, gives commuting alpha, f and g squares for the maps induced by u_i, including the connecting maps. These naturality squares depend only on the derived morphisms.

At each bidegree take the coproduct of the individual D and E terms. The direct-sum functor in a Grothendieck abelian category is exact: express the sum as the filtered colimit of finite sums and use AB5. Hence it preserves the three defining exact sequences and makes X an exact couple. Let Y be the target couple. Define T_D and T_E by coproduct descent. Every couple-morphism square reduces, after precomposition with a coproduct inclusion, to the corresponding individual naturality square. D vanishes when the truncation index is below a, since that truncated derived object is zero; exact sums preserve zero. E vanishes at negative first indices by connectivity of RF on degree-zero objects and the natural shift identifications.

For each n the canonical map from the n-th lower truncation to K_i induces an isomorphism on derived homology in degree n: its cone has lower bound n+1, and the derived functor preserves this lower bound. The individual canonical D-to-abutment isomorphisms, summed over i, give eX; the target gives eY. The truncation inclusion is natural, so each individual square commutes. Check the displayed coproduct-descent equality by precomposing with every inclusion, then cancel eX. This proves the required equation at every n, without assuming the abutment comparison is invertible.

For each nonnegative p and integer r, compose the single-functor shift comparison, the shift comparison for RF, and the homology shift comparison to identify E^{p,r} with H^p RF(H^r(-)[0]). These are natural isomorphisms. Sum their components for the source to obtain s, and use the target component for t. Naturality makes the individual E squares commute. Check the displayed E equation on each coproduct inclusion and apply the coproduct universal property. Empty families give the zero source couple and satisfy the same formulas.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_coproduct_truncation_couple
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} A]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} A]
    {B : Type uB} [Category.{v} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} B]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wB} B]
    (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F]
    (I : Type v) (K : I → DerivedCategory A) (S : DerivedCategory A)
    (u : ∀ i, K i ⟶ S) (a : ℤ)
    (hK : ∀ (i : I) (r : ℤ), r < a →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A r).obj (K i)))
    (hS : ∀ r : ℤ, r < a → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A r).obj S)) :
    ∃ (X Y : BigradedExactCouple B 0) (T : BigradedExactCouple.CoupleMorphism X Y),
      (∀ p r : ℤ, r < a → IsZero (X.D p r)) ∧
      (∀ p r : ℤ, r < a → IsZero (Y.D p r)) ∧
      (∀ p r : ℤ, p < 0 → IsZero (X.E p r)) ∧
      (∀ p r : ℤ, p < 0 → IsZero (Y.E p r)) ∧
      ∃ (eX : ∀ n : ℤ, X.D 0 n ≅
          ∐ (fun i ↦ (F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B n).obj
            (K i)))
        (eY : ∀ n : ℤ, Y.D 0 n ≅
          (F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B n).obj S),
        (∀ n : ℤ, Sigma.desc (fun i ↦
          (F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B n).map (u i)) =
            (eX n).inv ≫ T.tD 0 n ≫ (eY n).hom) ∧
        ∀ (p : ℕ) (r : ℤ),
          ∃ (s : X.E p r ≅ ∐ (fun i ↦
              (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0 ⋙ F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙
                DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B (p : ℤ)).obj
                  ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A r).obj (K i))))
            (t : Y.E p r ≅
              (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0 ⋙ F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙
                DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B (p : ℤ)).obj
                  ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A r).obj S)),
            T.tE p r = s.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i ↦
              (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0 ⋙ F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙
                DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B (p : ℤ)).map
                  ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A r).map (u i))) ≫ t.inv
